title: Idli / Dosa with Coconut Chutney
description: South Indian-style steamed rice cakes or crispy crepes widely available due to Tamil and other settler communities. Served with coconut chutney and mild sambar, reflecting the islands' multi-cultural breakfast culture.
steps: Steam idlis or cook thin dosas on a hot tawa.
Grind fresh coconut chutney with chillies and temper.
Serve hot with chutney and optional sambar.

fullIngredients.name: Idli or dosa batter (rice + urad dal)
Fresh coconut, green chillies, curry leaves for chutney

tip: Common at tiffin centres in Port Blair and larger islands.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Common at tiffin centres in Port Blair and larger islands.

title: Panta Bhat with Small Fish
time: Prep: 5 minutes + overnight soak | Cook: 10 minutes
description: Bengali-influenced fermented leftover rice soaked overnight, often eaten with small fried fish, salt, onion and green chilli. A cooling, everyday breakfast among Bengali settler communities.
steps: Soak cooked rice in water overnight.
Drain lightly in the morning.
Serve with lightly fried small fish, salt and raw onion/chilli.
tip: Traditionally a simple, hydrating summer breakfast.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditionally a simple, hydrating summer breakfast.

title: Andaman Fish Curry
description: The islands' everyday staple — fresh local fish (snapper, kingfish, reef fish) simmered in coconut milk with turmeric, mustard seeds, curry leaves and a touch of tamarind. Styles vary by community (Bengali mustard-based or South Indian coconut-based).
steps: Marinate fish lightly with turmeric and salt.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves; sauté aromatics.
Add spices, coconut milk and tamarind; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish and cook until just done. Serve with steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Turmeric, chilli powder, mustard seeds, curry leaves

tip: Use the freshest catch possible; do not overcook the fish.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Use the freshest catch possible; do not overcook the fish.

title: Coconut Prawn Curry
description: Juicy prawns cooked in a creamy coconut-milk gravy with curry leaves, ginger and mild spices. A tropical island classic that balances sweetness of prawns with gentle heat.
steps: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and curry leaves.
Add spices and a little water or thin coconut milk.
Add prawns and cook briefly.
Pour thick coconut milk and simmer gently until prawns are cooked.

fullIngredients.name: Curry leaves, turmeric, mild chilli powder

tip: Do not boil vigorously after adding thick coconut milk.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Do not boil vigorously after adding thick coconut milk.

title: Crab Curry / Crab Masala
description: Mud crab or local crab cooked in a rich onion-tomato-coconut masala. Messy, spicy and deeply flavourful — a signature island seafood experience.
steps: Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and spices into a thick masala.
Add tomato and cook until soft.
Add crabs and a little water or coconut milk; cover and cook until shells turn red and meat is done.
Finish with fresh coriander.

fullIngredients.name: Coconut (grated or milk), chilli powder, turmeric

tip: Eat with hands; the joy is in extracting the meat.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Eat with hands; the joy is in extracting the meat.

title: Vegetable Coconut Stew / Chilli Curry
description: Mild coconut-milk based vegetable curry with local produce (pumpkin, drumstick, beans, etc.) and green chillies. One of the more authentic vegetarian preparations available on the islands.
steps: Temper mustard and curry leaves.
Add onion, vegetables and a little water; cook until almost tender.
Pour coconut milk and simmer gently.
Season and serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chillies, curry leaves, mustard seeds

tip: Keep spices light to let the coconut and vegetables shine.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keep spices light to let the coconut and vegetables shine.

title: Grilled Lobster
description: Fresh lobster split and grilled with butter, garlic, chilli and lemon. A beach-shack and restaurant favourite on Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and around Port Blair, highlighting the natural sweetness of the seafood.
steps: Split lobster lengthwise and clean.
Brush with butter-garlic-chilli mixture.
Grill over charcoal or in a hot oven until flesh is opaque and slightly charred.
Serve with lemon wedges.

fullIngredients.name: Butter or oil, garlic, chilli, lemon

tip: Best when the lobster is extremely fresh.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Best when the lobster is extremely fresh.

title: Bamboo Chicken
description: Chicken marinated with local spices and herbs, stuffed into a hollow bamboo and slow-roasted over an open fire. An indigenous-style preparation that imparts a unique smoky, earthy flavour.
steps: Marinate chicken thoroughly.
Stuff into cleaned bamboo and seal the ends.
Roast slowly over open fire, turning occasionally, until cooked through.
Open bamboo and serve the aromatic chicken.

fullIngredients.name: Local spices, garlic, ginger, green chillies

tip: Traditionally cooked during outdoor gatherings or forest treks.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditionally cooked during outdoor gatherings or forest treks.

title: Macher Jhol (Bengali-style Fish Curry)
description: Light mustard-oil based fish curry with potatoes and cauliflower or other vegetables, seasoned with panch phoron and green chillies. Popular among the large Bengali settler population.
steps: Lightly fry fish pieces in mustard oil.
Temper panch phoron; add vegetables and turmeric.
Add water to make a light gravy; simmer.
Return fish and cook gently. Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil, panch phoron, turmeric, green chillies

tip: Keep the gravy thin and light — classic Bengali style.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Keep the gravy thin and light — classic Bengali style.

title: Fish Fry / Fish Pakora
description: Fresh fish pieces marinated with spices and either shallow-fried or coated in besan batter and deep-fried. A ubiquitous beach and market snack across the islands.
steps: Marinate fish with spices and lemon.
For fry: shallow-fry until crisp.
For pakora: coat in spiced besan batter and deep-fry.
Serve hot with chutney or lemon.

fullIngredients.name: Fish fillets or small whole fish
Besan (for pakora version), oil for frying

title: Squid Fry
description: Tender squid rings or pieces tossed with turmeric, chilli, pepper and curry leaves, then quickly fried. A popular coastal snack and starter.
steps: Marinate squid briefly with spices.
Heat oil, add curry leaves, then squid.
Stir-fry on high heat until just cooked and slightly crisp.
Serve immediately.

fullIngredients.name: Turmeric, chilli powder, black pepper, salt

tip: Overcooking makes squid rubbery — keep the cooking time short.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Overcooking makes squid rubbery — keep the cooking time short.

title: Coconut Ladoo
description: Simple sweet made from freshly grated coconut and jaggery or sugar, rolled into small balls. A traditional island treat that highlights the abundant local coconut.
steps: Cook grated coconut with jaggery until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides.
Add cardamom if using.
Cool slightly and roll into small ladoos.
tip: Use fresh coconut for the best flavour and texture.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Use fresh coconut for the best flavour and texture.

title: Banana Chips
description: Thinly sliced raw banana deep-fried until crisp and lightly salted. A popular local snack influenced by South Indian traditions and widely available in markets.
steps: Peel and thinly slice the banana.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.
Drain, sprinkle salt and store in an airtight container.
tip: Best when made fresh; they lose crispness over time.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Best when made fresh; they lose crispness over time.
